title: Aggregation-induced radical
content: Over the past three decades, organic semiconductors have achieved remarkable progress in various optoelectronic fields. Traditionally, the electronic ground state of the classic donor–acceptor (D–A) type organic semiconductors was considered a closed-shell singlet, with electron spin resonance signals widely attributed to impurities, defects, or external doping. However, the group of Yuan Li discovered that D–A organic semiconductors exhibit an intrinsic open-shell quinoidal diradical singlet ground state and thermally excited triplet state in 2017 for the first time (Y. Li et al., J. Phys. Chem. C, 2017, 121, 8579–8588) and further proposed a new concept of aggregation-induced radical (AIR) in 2019 (J. Zhou et al., Sci. China: Chem., 2019, 62, 1656–1665). In 2021, the mixed-solvent experiment further disclosed the AIR mechanism as the key driving force for the formation and stabilization of these open-shell D–A diradicals (Z. Chen et al., J. Phys. Chem. Lett., 2021, 12, 9783–9790). Differing from the 118-year-old and numerous Chichibabin-type diradicaloids stabilized by the recovery of aromaticity, AIR represents a new quinoid–diradical stabilized through ground-state electron transfer and enhanced intermolecular π–π interactions in the aggregated state, rather than the recovery of aromaticity. This review systematically summarizes Li's recent research progress on the AIR mechanism, multi-dimensional experimental evidence, diverse potential applications and future development directions, aiming to provide a comprehensive understanding of this emerging research field on the open-shell ground state of D–A materials and guide the design of novel materials for organic electronic and spintronic devices.
